particularites.text: Abbott is a long-standing « Dividend King » (54 consecutive years of dividend increases, S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats). Distribution policy is structural and takes priority in capital allocation, independently of the M&A cycle.

clesRetenues: Q David Roman (Goldman Sachs) - guidance philosophy and how de-risked the outlook is: management explains that it has included Exact Sciences in the comparable base for transparency, made conservative choices on the respiratory season, and cites three growth drivers (MedTech/pharma sustainability, Core Lab/Nutrition recovery, Exact Sciences integration).

Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - deceleration in organic growth excluding Exact Sciences: Ford replies that devices and pharma remain solid, acknowledges one-off challenges within the diversified portfolio, and stresses the ability to meet the overall commitments despite variations by business.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - CGM market weakness, prescription trends, Libre growth, timing of the non-insulin-dependent type 2 sensors and of the dual ketone/glucose sensor: management sets out a bullish long-term view (70-80M potential patients vs 10-12M today), and cites several reimbursement catalysts ahead, including non-insulin-dependent type 2 CMS coverage.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore ISI) - sustainability of Cologuard growth and international expansion: Ford stresses strong demand, under-penetration (50M Americans not screened), international expansion plans, colonoscopy capacity constraints, and rising retests (25% of tests, 500K per year).

Q Matt Taylor (Jefferies) - Structural Heart trends and impact of the left atrial appendage occlusion programme: management notes the transfer of LAA devices into the EP business, competitive intensity in mitral, high-single-digit annual growth expected, and the end of enrolment in the Catalyst trial.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - confidence in the Nutrition volume recovery and portfolio strategy: Ford describes targeted price cuts with volume elasticity analysis, early positive signs on Ensure, weekly monitoring, and a commitment to long-term value creation.

Q Joanne Wuensch (Citi) - macro risks from the Middle East conflict on costs and patient volumes: management indicates a currently minimal impact, active cost-monitoring teams, no observed decline in demand, and logistics constraints requiring better regional positioning of inventory.

Q Josh Jennings (TD Cowen) - detail on the EP franchise, Volt's international performance and US launch timing: Ford describes limited launch phases for Volt and TactiFlex Duo, highlights the conscious sedation and durability advantages, and projects an acceleration exceeding market growth (mid-to-high-teens).

Q Marie Thibault (BTIG) - Core Lab trajectory by geography and market share gain dynamics: management reports China stable (vs -15% to -30% previously), high-single-digit growth in the US with retention rates >90% and win rates >55%, Europe at mid/high single digit, and a mid-single-digit expectation for the year.

Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - risk of a deceleration in US procedure volumes in the face of hospital sector concerns: Ford dismisses that risk, noting that it is Medicare (not Medicaid) that drives device procedures, inelastic demand for high-acuity products, and stable diagnostic test volumes across all states.

Q Robbie Marcus (JPMorgan) - level of confidence in the H2 acceleration and key drivers: Ford expresses strong confidence, citing four main drivers (nutrition, electrophysiology, core lab diagnostics, cancer diagnostics) collectively representing 80% of the projected acceleration.

Q Larry Biegelsen (Wells Fargo) - Libre US/international trends, CGM outlook, timing of the dual ketone-glucose sensor and type 2 coverage: Ford confirms that reimbursement expansion is the main catalyst, US Medicare type 2 coverage could unlock 10 million beneficiaries, and a 5th manufacturing plant is planned.

Q Vijay Kumar (Evercore ISI) - visibility on Exact Sciences growth, contribution from the care gap programmes, positioning against blood-based colorectal screening: Ford confirms mid-teens annual growth (mid-teens), the care gap programmes ramping up in H2, and a complementary stool + blood test portfolio.

Q Matt Taylor (Jefferies) - EP market dynamics, growth ambitions, AF market trajectory, share gain potential: Ford avoids precise share targets but commits to outgrowing the market in H2, with Volt 2.0 adoption and the international rollout of TactiFlex Duo driving growth.

Q Travis Steed (BofA) - portfolio positioning for 2027 growth given easier comps and product launches: Ford reaffirms a sustainable total revenue growth target of 7%, noting that only five healthcare companies above 30 Md$ of revenue achieve it.

Q Josh Jennings (TD Cowen) - timing of the Structural Heart recovery, strategic initiatives for the US franchise, 2027 outlook: Ford expects mid/high-single-digit growth by year-end through personnel changes and repositioning, with the international team already posting double-digit growth.

Q Joanne Wuensch (Citi) - Nutrition acceleration trajectory, WIC contract updates, new product launches: Ford notes 125 M$ of sequential quarterly growth, the best international paediatric performance in two years, and new launches (collagen protein shake, creatine-enriched formulas).

Q Marie Thibault (BTIG) - market appetite for Amulet 360, competitive challenges in left atrial appendage occlusion: Ford emphasises market share capture rather than market growth, and the transfer of the LAA portfolio to the EP division for a complete procedural offering.

engagementsStructurants.engagement: Sustainable consolidated total revenue growth target of ~7% targeted for 2027 despite a broader base (management cites only 5 healthcare companies >30 Md$ of revenue reaching that pace).

pointsCles: Q2 26: sales $12.59B (+13.0% reported incl. Exact Sciences; +4.8% comparable, an acceleration vs the prior two quarters), adjusted EPS $1.31 above guidance midpoint and consensus; adjusted GM 58.0% (+100bp, mix incl. Exact + margin initiatives); FY adjusted EPS guidance raised to $5.45-5.60.

Second-half acceleration rests on 4 named businesses carrying ~80% of the trajectory shift - Nutrition (WIC leadership regained, Ensure US consumption up double-digit), Electrophysiology (Volt 2.0 US full release in Q3, TactiFlex Duo intl, Europe EP +20%, aim to outgrow the market and recapture share), Core Lab (US +7.5%, hospital labs +13%, China VBP drag fading from ~-30% to mid-single-digit), Cancer Diagnostics (Cologuard mid-teens, ACS 'preferred' designation, care-gap programs ramping in H2).

Libre/CGM read: $2B quarter (+9.5%) is the 'plateau' rate of ~8-9% absent a major reimbursement expansion; catalysts queued - US type-2 non-insulin (~10M Medicare lives, 'multibillion-dollar', possibly this fall), ~7 major international basal markets in discussion; Libre Duo (dual glucose-ketone, world first) CE-marked with US filing in final-stage talks; a 5th ~$1B sensor plant under planning.

Procedure-volume fears rebutted from Abbott's own diagnostics telemetry (no slowdown even in high-ACA-disenrollment states; Medicare, not Medicaid, funds >2/3 of US cardio); Structural Heart soft spot is US mitral execution (fix by Q4, intl double-digit, TAVR +30% H1); Amulet 360 filed (competitor holds ~90% of a $2B LAA market - relaunch/share-capture setup for 2027).

hypothese.summary: Q2 26 adjusted EPS above consensus and FY26 guidance raised, but the GAAP/adjusted gap considerably widened by the Exact Sciences integration (amortisation, integration costs, legal provision). Thesis intact: acceleration expected in H2 with the one-off acquisition-related costs progressively fading.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Diversified four-legged healthcare portfolio (Nutrition, Diagnostics, Established Pharma, Medical Devices) compounding mid-single-digit organic, with a structural accelerator: Exact Sciences (closed 23/03/2026, ~3bn incremental 2026 revenue) makes Abbott the leader in colorectal-cancer screening via Cologuard - a mid-teens-growth recurring market. Q2 26 showed classic year-1 acquisition mechanics: margin dilution and one-off integration costs, with FY26 adjusted-EPS guidance nonetheless RAISED to 5.45-5.60.

== THESIS READ ==
- Integration-fade is the 2027 earnings driver: one-off costs dissipate, synergies ramp - the model's margin-expansion spine. Watch: quarterly integration-cost disclosures shrinking on schedule.
- Cancer-screening growth (Cologuard mid-teens+) re-rates the Diagnostics leg. Watch: Cologuard volume prints and competitive blood-based entrants.
- Balance sheet: ~20bn bridge facility took net debt from 4.4bn to a ~24bn peak; deleveraging on ~9-10bn/yr operating cash flow. Watch: post-closing balance sheet confirmation - the modeling decision flagged at setup.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Base = GAAP retreated for true one-offs only; Abbott's 'adjusted' (guidance metric) excludes intangible amortization/integration costs - basis mismatch documented (Omnium 4.30 vs guided 5.48+ for 2026). Comparable-sales guidance includes Exact Sciences in both bases. priorEPS null (young fiche).

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 49.3bn, EBIT 9.1bn, net 7.5bn (ETR 16% normative; FY25 actual ~14% documented). 2027-2030: ~7.5%/yr revenue, margin rebuild post-integration, net debt 24 -> 10bn. finNet modest (facility interest net of cash income) - to firm up post-closing. Watch: Libre franchise momentum; China VBP pressure on Established Pharma.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Oct); integration-cost fade evidence; Cologuard prints; 2027 guidance (Jan) - first clean combined-year frame.

ancrages.moteur: The one-off integration and inventory step-up costs tied to the Exact Sciences acquisition ($532M pretax in H1 26) fade progressively as the integration advances, with no recurrence beyond 2026-2027.

Cologuard and the Cancer Diagnostics segment (ex-Exact Sciences) are growing at a structurally faster pace (~13% comparable) than the rest of the Diagnostics portfolio, driving consolidated revenue growth across the whole projection horizon.

Once the Exact Sciences one-off integration costs have faded (from 2027), scale synergies and the operating leverage of the Medical Devices/Diagnostics portfolio restore a trajectory of gradual EBIT margin expansion.

The peak in net debt tied to the financing of the Exact Sciences acquisition (bridge facility ~$20Md) is progressively repaid out of the free cash flow generated (~$9-10Md/yr of operating cash flow), temporarily at the expense of buybacks.
Normative effective tax rate taken at 16%, in line with the rate excluding specified items communicated by management over several consecutive quarters (15.0%-16.6%).

RESCOPING for Exact Sciences (close 23/03): adjusted EPS 5,38-5,58$, incorporating -0,20$ of acquisition-related dilution (5,675-0,20=5,475: a pure scope rescoping, not an operating revision). Comparable growth 6,5/7,5% unchanged.
FY26 raised: adjusted EPS $5.45-$5.60 (vs $5.38-$5.58 previously); comparable sales growth reaffirmed at 6.5%-7.5% (includes Exact Sciences in the comparable base for both years).

rupture.motif: Acquisition d'Exact Sciences bouclée le 23/03/2026, sans retraitement des comparatifs 2025. Le périmètre et le stock d'incorporels amortissables sont discontinus : amortissement trimestriel 420 M$ (2Q25) → 658 M$ (2Q26), intérêts nets 50 → 299 M$, nouveau segment Cancer Diagnostics. La série des postes amort-incorporels-acquisition et acquisition-cession-frais ne se projette pas à travers cette borne sans retraitement.
